title: Contract teachers’ announced national stoppage and proposed sit-ins, 16 January
reason: Opened article documents a call and planned follow-on sit-ins, not their occurrence or attendance.
notes: The 26 December 2021 sit-in mentioned in the same article is outside this unit.

title: Tax staff one-day strike reported for 5 January
reason: The opened report describes a work stoppage only; it does not document a public gathering or turnout.
notes: The union’s “most employees” claim and the sector workforce are not gathering attendance. Reconsider only if direct evidence of a qualifying public assembly is found.

title: SAFI national tax staff strike, 18–20 January
reason: Opened reports describe a work stoppage and office shutdown, not a public sit-in, march, or gathering. A 96% Annaba strike response rate is not public-gathering turnout.
notes: Direct state-facing labor demands are documented, but a qualifying public assembly of at least 50 is not.

title: Interprovincial taxi drivers’ work stoppage preceding the 23 January sit-in
reason: The report documents a work stoppage, not whether it included a public gathering or how many people assembled.
notes: The separate 23 January sit-in is retained as candidate algeria_2022-01_C002.

title: Tizi Ouzou bakers’ strike and bread-supply disruption
reason: Opened reports document an occupational stoppage and supply effects, but no public gathering or attendance estimate.
notes: Echorouk describes an open-ended Tizi Ouzou bakers’ strike; Liberté confirms the association call and near-total bakery closures but gives no precise demands or end date. The Liberté account’s local Bouzeguène supply adaptation does not prove the strike ended across the wilaya.

title: UNOA indefinite national lawyer strike and court boycott, starting 13 January
reason: The opened report documents a judicial strike/boycott and empty/disrupted courtrooms, not a public march, sit-in, or other gathering with attendance.
notes: Reported 100% boycott rates and numbers of licensed lawyers are not turnout. The article says authorities had not reacted through 16 January. No gathering event is inferred from the national boycott.
